findings.title: Concurrent due-wait polls can overwrite the native re-admission owner and strand its successful launch
findings.evidence: A due attempt with unit Some, session None, and native_wait Some sends every polling step into prepare_managed. The initial waiting Workflow record is not claimed exclusively before its asynchronous source calls. prepare_managed unconditionally replaces that snapshot with self.read at line 1409, and only checks the active index and unit identity; it does not require the same waiting record version/native_wait or reject a newly in-flight preparation. It then clears native_wait and persists another record version. The earlier invocation requires its own Workflow record version to remain unchanged before binding the returned Session. The per-unit NativeSessions mutex serializes native starts, but does not protect these preceding Workflow writes or their outer PreparationGuards.
causal_interleaving: A and B both read the same due waiting attempt; pause B in the poll inputs call at lines 1602-1609.
A clears native_wait and persists at 1439-1444, then holds its native_version helper before Session registration.
Release B. Its unit still has no Session, and self.read at 1409 adopts A's new record with native_wait already None. It persists a further Workflow version and waits for the same native start mutex.

Allow A to finish native preparation. If it launches, the actual Unit and Session become bound at NativeSessions lines 349 and 417-429, but A's refresh_owners at 1484 rejects B's Workflow version. The durable Workflow remains unbound. A's outer PreparationGuard has session None and cannot retire the now Session-bound Unit.

B subsequently fails the original Session-less ExecutionAuthority check; its error branch can publish WaitingHuman while leaving the live Unit/Session unbound. Ordinary polls now return the unbound recovery hold instead of monitoring the actual successful launch.

If A instead returns another quota/capacity wait, its binding/update CAS fails for the same reason; its still-armed Session-less outer guard can retire the healthy waiting Unit as Lost. Neither outcome is caused by actual native transport loss.
findings.impact: Healthy concurrent polling can require explicit recovery or an unnecessary fresh attempt even though native preparation/launch ownership was preserved. This does not demonstrate duplicate model input or a false result approval: the lower-level per-unit mutex and ledger fences remain effective. It is a concrete availability/currency defect in the newly connected wait consumer, rather than an absent future Runtime integration.

contract_evidence.requirement: R3 immutable attempt binding and record-version CAS
R5 bounded quota recovery, preserved continuation and waiting semantics

findings.minimal_fix: Atomically claim the exact due waiting Workflow record/attempt/unit before re-admission. A CAS loser or observer that sees native_wait already cleared must return Waiting without writing or arming a retirement guard for the winner. Preserve the winning invocation's committed version/token through re-admission and binding; do not adopt a competing in-flight Workflow by unconditional reread. The initial newly reserved Unit reload may remain separately justified by its own successful atomic reservation.
causal_controls: Use the real managed Registry/Workflow fixture. First obtain a genuine Session-less quota/capacity wait, then make its bounded recheck due and permit capacity recovery.

Use source and version-helper barriers to force the listed interleaving with two WorkflowEngine instances sharing the same Registry/Store. Assert one native start/input, exactly one durable Workflow Session binding to the launched Unit, no unexpected Lost/WaitingHuman, and observer/no-winner writes do not revoke the owner.

Repeat with the winning native recheck returning Waiting again: its Unit must stay open and WaitingQuota/WaitingCapacity with intact waiter/lease accounting, not become Lost because of the other poll.

Retain normal sequential wait recovery, initial concurrent native start exclusion, cancellation and fresh terminal-capacity retry controls. An omission of the waiting-claim/current-version check must fail the actual Workflow binding or waiter-state assertion.
findings.verification: Verified from immutable production control flow and a feasible explicitly ordered interleaving; no test/build/probe was executed by this reviewer.

reports.review_kind: Independent read-only STRICT preliminary component source review

findings.title: Managed subscriptions never publish the durable quota/capacity wait reason
findings.evidence: NativeStatus starts with wait_reason=None. No watch-channel producer in this pinned source assigns wait_reason thereafter. A Codex usageLimitExceeded notification with willRetry=true durably changes the live unit to WaitingQuota/Some(Quota), but the subsequent send_modify assigns only authority and diagnostic. Terminal persistence assigns Some(Quota) or Some(Capacity) for the corresponding interrupted dispositions, while the final send_modify again omits wait_reason. NativeSessions::status overlays the durable unit's wait_reason, but NativeAdapter::subscribe forwards the unrefreshed NativeStatus directly, including its initial value for a late subscriber.
causal_sequence: Start a managed Codex session and subscribe through the managed adapter.
Receive a correlated usageLimitExceeded notification whose willRetry is true; mark_execution_quota_retry commits wait_reason=Quota.
The emitted watch value reports the same native turn and a quota diagnostic, but execution.wait_reason remains None. A synchronous adapter.status for the same handle reports Some(Quota).
A terminal quota/capacity interruption preserves the disagreement because terminal watch publication omits wait_reason as well.
findings.impact: The existing public subscription path cannot reliably expose the new structured wait state. A subscriber can continue treating an exhausted retained turn as running while synchronous status says it is waiting, and must parse diagnostic prose to reconstruct the state. Current Workflow::poll uses synchronous status, so this finding does not claim that its quota wait/retry branch fails, that results are corrupted, or that capacity is incorrectly classified as work failure.
findings.recommended_change: Publish an internally consistent NativeStatus from the current persisted unit whenever quota retry, terminal persistence, retirement or other authoritative state changes are emitted. At minimum, copy unit.wait_reason alongside authority/work/disposition/cleanup in the quota and terminal producer updates; ensure recovery clears it. Alternatively refresh the durable fields before each adapter subscription emission. Preserve the retained native Session/turn without resending input.
proposed_causal_controls_not_executed: An account-free managed-adapter fixture emits a held correlated usageLimitExceeded/willRetry=true notification. Compare subscription.execution.wait_reason and adapter.status.execution.wait_reason; both must equal Some(Quota), and assert there is still exactly one native input/turn.
Repeat the comparison for terminal QuotaInterrupted and CapacityInterrupted, including a subscriber created after the terminal update.
Complete a retained retry successfully and assert both views clear wait_reason without creating a replacement native turn.
findings.confidence: Verified by the complete pinned-source assignment search and producer-to-consumer tracing; no test was run.

additional_verified_source_observations: Managed Registry construction requires explicit claude/codex provider mapping, preserves configured agent aliases, resolves the configured native executable, and shares a RuntimeOwner-backed NativeSessions registry. Generic start remains unavailable for the managed adapter, while the actual AgentAdapter managed vtable path is used by Workflow.

Managed Workflow admission stores the semantic pre-Session Unit reference with Task projection and Workflow phase reservation in one transaction. It checks Workflow/Project/Goal/Context versions and actor-to-unit-kind binding before native preparation.

The managed adapter compares its native input to the durable ContextVersion and running Workflow attempt, including agent alias, phase, semantic Unit identity, revision, source hashes and payload; caller-provided input cannot independently substitute for that frame.

Workflow polling handles confirmed live native retry without resending input and handles terminal quota/capacity interruption by retiring the phase attempt and admitting a fresh execution unit/worktree/resource set. The due-time pre-Session wait path uses the persisted Context input and the same not-yet-launched unit; that is not reuse of a previously launched executor attempt.

Workflow publication now requires a private real ResultStore proof produced by retained manifest/graph verification, then compares the complete artifact snapshot in the coordinated publication transaction. Artifact, Unit finalization, Task, Workflow and Context updates retain CAS rollback behavior.

Readonly managed review uses a private ResultSnapshot provenance object and verifies its semantic unit, exact retained SHA, tracked content and read-only source/Git tree before launch, before gate evaluation and before accepting passed review evidence. This is a cooperative source-consumption guarantee, not a same-UID security sandbox.
limits: No builds, tests, native agents, accounts, authentication/configuration probes, network operations, Docker operations or process signals were performed. Proposed causal controls are not observed passing tests.

This review used only fixed git source objects at the stated source/baseline/contract commits and did not inspect dirty source, subsequent commits, peer reports, merged review artifacts or progress documents.

Production Sources/Gates, readonly finalization closure, Runtime operational CLI, cleanup backends and final native compatibility/concurrency qualification remain incomplete as explicitly scoped by the parent. Their absence alone is not counted as a finding and this verdict is not Phase2 approval.
Actual Claude/Codex authentication, settings, required hooks, sandbox compatibility, subscription exhaustion/reset and four simultaneous native Tasks on macOS/Linux remain unverified.

Configured operational concurrency limits and completed due-time quota recovery require later integration/qualification; source fixture inspection does not establish either native behavior or CLI readiness.

Retained source trees are not a security boundary against intentional chmod/raw filesystem bypass by the same user; external effects and best-effort cleanup remain outside complete process-reclamation guarantees.
